articles.heading: The Nature and Objectives of the Game
articles.content: The game of chess is played between two opponents who move pieces alternately on a square board called a chessboard. The player with the white pieces commences the game. A player is said to have the move when his opponent's move has been made. The objective of each player is to place the opponent's king under attack in such a way that the opponent has no legal move. The player who achieves this goal is said to have checkmated the opponent's king and to have won the game.

articles.heading: The Chessboard and its Squares
articles.content: The chessboard is composed of an 8x8 grid of 64 equal squares alternately light (white) and dark (black). The chessboard is placed between the players in such a way that the near corner square to the right of each player is white. The eight columns of squares running from one player to the other are called files. The eight rows of squares running from side to side are called ranks.

articles.heading: The Pieces
articles.content: At the beginning of the game one player has 16 light-coloured pieces (white pieces) and the other has 16 dark-coloured pieces (black pieces). These pieces are as follows: a king, a queen, two rooks, two bishops, two knights, and eight pawns.

articles.heading: Touch Move Rule
articles.content: Each move must be made with one hand only. Provided that he first expresses his intention (for example by saying 'j'adoube' or 'I adjust'), the player having the move may adjust one or more pieces on their squares. After the player has moved a piece by releasing it, the move cannot be changed.

articles.heading: Late Arrival of a Player
articles.content: Any player who arrives at the chessboard after the start of the session shall lose the game unless the arbiter decides otherwise. Thus the default time is 0 minutes. The rules of a competition may specify a different default time.

articles.heading: The Draw – Stalemate
articles.content: A game is drawn when the player to move has no legal move and his king is not in check. This is called stalemate. A game is also drawn when a position has arisen in which neither player can checkmate the opponent's king with any series of legal moves. This is called a dead position.

articles.heading: Draw by Agreement
articles.content: The game is drawn upon agreement between the two players during the game. Offering a draw: either player may offer a draw. The offer may be made after the player has made a move on the chessboard, then pressing the clock. An offer may not be withdrawn and remains valid until the opponent accepts it, rejects it orally, rejects it by touching a piece, or the game is concluded in some other way.

articles.heading: Draw – Threefold Repetition
articles.content: The game is drawn, upon a correct claim by a player having the move, when the same position for at least the third time (not necessarily by a repetition of moves) is about to appear, if the player first writes the move on his scoresheet and declares to the arbiter his intention to make this move, or the same position has appeared, at least three times.
